title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Comprehensive Addendum
author: Aria Chen
summary: Addendum to the canonical on-call and incident response playbook: clarifications on handoff, communications, and additional runbooks for model-serving incidents.
content:
Purpose

This addendum extends the On-call & Incident Response Playbook with clarified handoff procedures, additional runbook steps for model-serving incidents (quantization/compatibility regressions), and refined customer communications templates used when rolling mitigations such as model reroutes are in effect. Apply these procedures in conjunction with the main playbook.

Handoff addendum (detailed checklist)

Outgoing on-call must complete the following items before formal handoff time:

- Post an entry in the on-call calendar with a 1-line status and link to the active Jira INC ticket (if any).
- Write a 5–10 bullet status note in #incidents: current severity, ongoing mitigations, last actions, and outstanding watch items (dashboards/queries).
- Attach or link any temporary scripts or quick commands used during the incident (e.g., `rictl` invocations).
- Confirm the incoming on-call has acknowledged and responded in Slack at least once before handoff time.
- If the outgoing on-call is unable to complete handoff (unplanned leave), the secondary or on-call lead must perform the handoff.

Extended runbooks (model-serving regressions and quantization issues)

1) Model quantization regression (new quantized model variant causing incorrect outputs or silent failures)
- Symptoms: Sudden increase in semantic errors in outputs, customer reports of hallucinations or mismatched tokenization, or increased application-level errors without 5xx.
- Immediate mitigation steps:
  a. Quarantine traffic by routing a percentage (e.g., 0-100%) away from quantized variant to the last-known-good float variant using the runtime console.
  b. Compare sample outputs using canary prompt set; run automated eval: `eval-runner --prompts ./canary/prompts.json --model float-variant --model quantized-variant --output ./evals`
  c. If outputs confirm regression, mark quantized variant as deprecated in catalog and unblock rollback to previous variant.
  d. Notify model-onboarding and applied-ml teams for root-cause triage (quantization script/bitwidth/config drift).
- Verification: Canary eval scores for semantic fidelity return to baseline and customer reports reduce.
- Owner: Applied ML + serving-runtime.

2) Model runtime compatibility failure after runtime upgrade
- Symptoms: Certain model families fail to load or crash at KV-cache restore, OOM during restore, or get stuck on warmup steps.
- Runbook:
  a. Check runtime and model-compatibility matrix in Runtime Console > Models > Compatibility.
  b. If incompatible, revert runtime to previous stable version in the affected cluster and pin models to the compatible runtime.
  c. If rolling back runtime is not feasible, route affected model families to a different cluster running compatible runtime.
  d. Roll forward with a canary set of models after fixing compatibility shims.
- Owner: Serving-runtime + infra.

Customer comms — clarifications for in-progress mitigations

- When mitigation is a traffic reroute (e.g., to fallback smaller model), include the following in public and customer messages:
  - Short explanation: We routed traffic to a fallback model variant to restore availability while we investigate.
  - Expected user impact: Slightly higher latency or lower context window for some requests; functional behavior remains supported.
  - ETA guidance: Provide monitoring-based ETA (e.g., monitoring shows errors reduced by 70%; targeted full recovery in 1-2 hours).
  - Offer: If a customer requires stricter fidelity, provide a contact path to request prioritized routing/tests.

Status page template (reroute mitigation example)

- Title: API Degraded — Fallback Routing Active
- Summary: We have routed a portion of traffic to a fallback model variant to restore request success rates. This reduces errors while we investigate a regression in the primary serving runtime.
- Impact: Some responses may have reduced context length or slightly different output characteristics. Availability is partially restored for most customers.
- What we've done: Enabled fallback routing, increased capacity in secondary region, and started a root-cause investigation.
- Next update: in 30 minutes or when status materially changes.

Communication checklist for CS and Solutions teams

- Use the standard email templates, but append the exact mitigation line and expected functional impact.
- If customers report data integrity concerns, escalate immediately to security and legal and do not speculate on cause in public messages.
- Offer a follow-up call for customers with > $10k monthly spend or critical SLAs.

Additional diagnostics snippets

- Compare canary outputs: `python tools/compare_outputs.py --base ./canary/float.json --candidate ./canary/quantized.json --metrics rouge_bleu_embedding`
- Check KV cache restore logs: `kubectl logs -n model-serving <pod> -c serving-runtime | grep -i \"kv restore\" -n`
- Quick model routing change via CLI: `rictl routing set --policy fallback --model-id <fallback> --percentage 50`

Training and game-day validation addendum

- For quarterly game days, require at least one scenario to validate the quantization regression runbook and one to validate the runtime compatibility runbook. Document the success criteria (canary eval passes, routing changes applied without errors).

Change log for this addendum

- 2026-03-01: Addendum published (clarified handoff checklist, added quantization and compatibility runbooks, refined comms templates).
notes: This addendum supplements the canonical playbook. Teams operating model-serving and applied-ml should cross-reference this page when updating model onboarding or quantization profiles.
